verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's Flow is documented as a way to "accept payments using customizable components – all through one simple integration". Flow for Mobile extends this to native checkout through the iOS and Android SDKs, and public keys are provided for client-side channels. Together this is a first-party embedded alternative, distinct from the separate Hosted Payment Page product. However, the evidence is mostly product-page marketing, and web embedding is implied by "components" rather than spelled out. Missing for 10: in-depth docs on how components are embedded and on customization options (styling, layout, events), plus independent or hands-on corroboration.
